sections.h2: Why is Ware County unlike the rest of south Georgia?
sections.html:
Ware County covers 908 square miles, more than any other county in Georgia, and a large block of that is wetland inside the Okefenokee Swamp and its federal refuge. Lawmakers carved it from Appling County on December 15, 1824, numbered it the state's 60th county and named it for Nicholas Ware, per Wikipedia.

Waycross is the county seat and its only incorporated city. Bickley, Ruskin, Jamestown and Telmore are unincorporated communities, so outside the city limits an address answers only to county rules. Neighbors are Bacon, Pierce, Brantley, Charlton, Clinch, Atkinson and Coffee counties, and Baker County, Florida touches the south.

Water runs three ways here. The Suwannee, St. Marys and Satilla river basins all drain parts of the county. Laura S. Walker State Park honors a local author and conservationist who promoted forest parks; the land was bought during the 1930s and deeded to Georgia in 1941.

Ware was once much bigger. Bacon, Charlton, Clinch, Coffee and Pierce counties were each formed partly from its territory. South Georgia State College and Coastal Pines Technical College both have Waycross campuses, and the elementary schools include Wacona, Center, Williams Heights, Memorial Drive, Ruskin and Waresboro. Public schooling runs through a single district: a preschool, six elementary schools, two middle schools and one high school, enrolling upward of 6,370 students. Discovery Montessori School and Lighthouse Christian Academy are private choices.

The city's name comes from its position at railroad junctions, with track leaving in six directions, and CSX still runs the Rice Yard sorting yard and shops there. The settlement dates from about 1820, was renamed Tebeauville in 1857, won the courthouse in 1873 and incorporated as Way Cross on March 3, 1874. In 2020 the city held 13,942 people and 6,775 housing units, with 18.7% of them empty. Four federal highways cross in town (1, 23, 82 and 84), and two historic districts carry National Register listings. Memorial Satilla Health treats most local patients, and a county-and-city airport sits northwest of downtown. NOAA figures show close to 50 inches of rain a year, heaviest from June to August, and with the Okefenokee so near, a buyer may ask how a given lot drains.

One local footnote ties the city to its tax rolls: in 1917 the Waycross city council opened municipal primaries to white women, the first town in Georgia to do so, because some of the largest property owners in town were women who wanted a say in how their tax dollars were spent. The Obediah Barber Homestead, seven miles south of the city, is another National Register property.

sections.h2: What are Ware County homes worth, and who lives in them?
sections.html:
The middle owner-occupied home here is valued at $109,500 for 2020-2024, close to a third of the $332,700 national figure, according to QuickFacts.

The county had 36,312 residents in 2010, 36,251 in 2020 and an estimate of 36,906 for 2025, and it holds 12,957 households. Population history is a long climb and a plateau: 8,811 in 1890, 22,957 in 1910, 37,180 in 1980 and just under 37,000 now. Census day in 2020 turned up 15,858 housing units, 13.9% of them vacant. Renters held 37.8% of the occupied ones, residents had a median age of 39.8, and 67.9% lived in urban areas. Vacancy near one in seven is high, and a balance left unpaid for several years can turn into a recorded lien.

sections.h2: Which Ware County offices send and collect the bill?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner bills and collects. The assessors set values, and the county commission and school board each choose a millage rate.

  • Commissioner's counter: 305 Oak Street, Suite 115A, Waycross, GA 31501. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1825, Waycross, GA 31502. The site header lists (912) 490-4305, and the office keeps weekday hours from half past eight to five.
  • Assessors: (912) 287-4383 according to the FAQ page, with written appeals directed to 305 Oak St., Suite 154.
  • Online parcel search and payment: warecountytax.com. Anyone whose lender escrows the tax should call the lender before paying, so the bill is not paid twice.
  • Recorded deeds: the Clerk of Superior Court, 800 Church Street.

Ask the commissioner whether a City of Waycross charge appears on your statement. The exemption list refers to city, county and school freezes, so city tax can matter for houses inside Waycross.

sections.h2: What does a late Ware County bill cost?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner expects to mail statements by September 15, and the due date is November 15. Manufactured homes follow a calendar of their own: January bills, April 1 payment, and a decal handed out once the tax is paid.

The FAQ spells out what happens after the due date for bills dated July 1, 2016 or later.

  • Interest accrues at the Federal Reserve prime rate plus 3%.
  • Each 120 days adds a 5% penalty, stopping at 20% of unpaid principal.
  • A homesteaded parcel with tax under $500 owes interest but no penalty.
  • Past 90 days, a FIFA lien can be recorded at the Clerk of Superior Court, where credit bureaus can read it.

Where an account stays open, a levy is possible. Sales take place at 305 Oak Street in the Board of Commissioners Room on a first Tuesday, following four weeks of notices in the Waycross Journal Herald. The county does not promise title, and a purchaser waits at least a year before using the land or collecting rent.

sections.h2: What homestead and tax relief does Ware County offer?
sections.html:
To qualify for homestead exemption you must own and occupy the house as of January 1, and the application goes to the Tax Assessor's office. Its pages print March 1 in one place and April 1 in another as the cutoff, so confirm with the assessors before filing. An approved exemption carries over each year.

  • Freeze exemptions lock the county, school and city operating-tax value at the prior year's level while you stay.
  • An extra local exemption for owners 62 and older with adjusted gross income of $24,000 or less takes up to $20,000 off the 40% assessed value.
  • A floating exemption for ages 62 and up with household income of $30,000 or less swaps out other state and county exemptions, and the county cautions that it may initially raise the bill.
  • Damaged timber: the commissioner's front page points to the TREES Act form from the Georgia Forestry Commission.

sections.h2: How can I challenge a Ware County valuation?
sections.html:
Appeals must be filed within 45 days after the date on your assessment notice, on grounds of taxability, value or uniformity. The size of the bill is not a ground.

After the assessors reconsider, the next step is the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, and then Superior Court on written notice. Another route is a return filed from January 1 to April 1 that names a different value.

sections.h2: What is the best way to sell a Ware County house with tax unpaid?
sections.html:
Get a payoff from the commissioner and let the closing agent send it from your proceeds. If a levy has been threatened, check the tax sale list on the county site, since a sale date can set your timeline.

A mobile home has a separate April 1 bill and decal, so keep that account apart from the land. A buyer who takes the property as it stands and accepts the title work can close fast. The commissioner also keeps an excess funds list, worth checking if money may be owed to you from an earlier sale.

faqs.q: Which month do Ware County real estate bills fall due?
faqs.a: November. The county aims to mail statements by mid-September, and manufactured homes are billed separately for April.

faqs.q: Can I pay a Ware County bill without going to Waycross?
faqs.a: Yes. Search the parcel and pay on warecountytax.com, or mail a check to P.O. Box 1825, Waycross, GA 31502. If your lender escrows the tax, check with the lender first.

faqs.q: Where is an appeal of a Ware County value sent?
faqs.a: To the Board of Tax Assessors at 305 Oak St., Suite 154, Waycross, within 45 days of the notice date.

faqs.q: Is there a penalty if only part of a Ware County bill is late?
faqs.a: Interest runs on the unpaid principal at prime plus 3%, and the 5% penalty steps (every 120 days, up to 20%) apply to what remains unpaid. Homesteaded parcels under $500 skip the penalty.

faqs.q: How do I avoid a Ware County tax sale on my house?
faqs.a: Clear the balance with the commissioner before the first-Tuesday sale. A lien that is satisfied drops off the sale list, and the office can quote a payoff.
